title: sre-weekly-update-2026-04-25
content:
SRE Weekly Update - 2026-04-25

Owner: Maya Patel
Team: Site Reliability Engineering (eng-sre)
Period: 2026-04-18 -> 2026-04-24

Summary highlights:
- Two customer-impacting incidents this week (see Incidents section).
- SLOs remain within target for availability but 99th percentile latency regressed for the text-generation route on evening traffic.
- On-call handoff process updated to include a quick triage checklist for cache-related errors.
- Began phased rollout of improved KV-cache eviction parameters to reduce cold-start latency for long-context requests.

Incidents:
1) INC-2026-0423: Increased 5xx rate on hosted API (2026-04-19 18:37 UTC -> 2026-04-19 19:12 UTC)
   - Impact: ~7% of requests to text-generation route returned 500/502 for ~35 minutes. Customers reported short bursts of failures and retry storms.
   - Root cause: a deploy rolled a change to the request path normalization that caused a rare nil-pointer in an upstream request validation library under specific multi-tenant header combinations.
   - Mitigation: Rollback to previous build and throttle retry rate via rate-limit temporary rule.
   - Post-incident actions: patch PR to validate headers defensively (GitHub:repo/infrastructure#412), add unit test for header permutations, update deploy checklist to include integration test on canary region.
   - Linked artifact: JIRA:INC-2026-0423

2) INC-2026-0424: KV-cache cold-start regression causing high p99 latency (2026-04-22 04:05 UTC -> 2026-04-22 06:40 UTC, intermittent residuals)
   - Impact: P99 latency for text-generation increased from 420ms -> 1.2s for a subset of traffic after autoscaler scaled up new replicas; observed customer complaints for interactive apps.
   - Root cause hypothesis: aggressive pod scaling combined with a change in cache shard assignment led to higher cache miss ratio on new replicas; cold-key population took longer than expected.
   - Mitigation: temporarily increased warm-pool minimum replicas and enabled a lightweight async prefetch of recent keys during bootstrap.
   - Post-incident actions: tune eviction thresholds, add metrics for cache population time and warm-pool readiness, run chaos test for scaled-up replicas.
   - Linked artifact: JIRA:INC-2026-0424, Confluence:sre/runbooks/cache-miss-analysis

SLO status and trends:
- Host API availability (user-facing success rate) 30d: 99.96% (target 99.9%).
- Text-generation p99 latency 7d: 1.02s (target 800ms) — regression observed after autoscaler changes; action plan below.
- Embeddings pipeline daily SLA: met.

Metrics to watch:
- Cache miss ratio by replica age (new metric added this week).
- Request error rate by deploy tag and header fingerprint.
- Warm-pool readiness time (new gauge).

On-call handoffs and rotation notes:
- Week on-call: 2026-04-18 -> 2026-04-24 primary: Liam Chen, secondary: Ava Rodriguez.
- Handoff notes captured in the on-call doc prior to shift change. Key items passed on:
  - Ongoing cache tuning experiment (DO NOT revert without consulting Maya).
  - Monitoring alert threshold lowered temporarily for 5xx surge alerts after recent incidents.
- New handoff checklist item: verify canary region deploy succeeded and perform smoke traffic against text-generation route.

Operational changes and runbooks:
- Added 'cache-population' troubleshooting section to the runtime runbook. See Confluence:sre/runbooks/cache-miss-analysis.
- Updated deploy checklist to include header permutation test to guard against validation regressions.
- Temporary measure: we have set a conservative autoscaler floor for dedicated pools to reduce cold-starts during peak PST hours.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Maya: Merge defensive header validation patch and add unit tests (ETA: 2026-04-27). Linked: GitHub:repo/infrastructure#412.
- Liam: Implement cache population latency metric and dashboard (ETA: 2026-05-02).
- Ava: Run two chaos experiments simulating rapid scale-up to validate warm-pool behavior (ETA: 2026-05-09).
- Noah: Review alert thresholds and rollback criteria for deploys that touch request-path code (ETA: 2026-04-30).

Meeting notes and decisions:
- Weekly SRE sync (2026-04-20): Decided to prioritize reducing p99 latency over marginal cost savings in autoscaler policy for the next 3 sprints.
- Incident review session (2026-04-21): Agreed on deploy checklist and to expand unit/integration test coverage for header handling.
- Postmortem follow-up assigned; next review on 2026-04-29.

Risks and blockers:
- Risk: If cache warm-up fixes are insufficient, customer-facing latency may persist during sustained scale events.
  Mitigation: expedite warm-pool improvements and consider pre-warming during predicted traffic windows.
- Blocker: dependency on library maintainers for a fix in request validation library; temporary defensive patch in place but long-term solution requires upstream coordination.

Notes to the team (informal):
- Please add any additional context or customer tickets to the linked JIRA items.
- If you see anomalies in canary after 10:00 PDT, escalate to primary on-call and tag the deploy.

Attachments and links:
- JIRA:INC-2026-0423
- JIRA:INC-2026-0424
- Confluence: sre/runbooks/cache-miss-analysis
- GitHub PR: repo/infrastructure#412

Next week focus:
- Complete header validation patch and deploy to canary.
- Implement cache population metrics and dashboards.
- Run chaos tests for rapid autoscaler scale-up and tune warm-pool behavior.

End of update.
